item.title: A Performative Control Approach to Day-to-Day Traffic Signal Retiming
item.description: arXiv:2610.19022v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conventional fixed-time traffic signal optimization and recent day-to-day signal retiming generally model route adaptation under prescribed route-choice behavior and origin-destination (OD) demand, while neglecting the fact that travelers' behavior can be performative to the signal control policy. A signal timing policy learned from historical traffic observations must therefore account for how its own deployment changes the distribution on which it will be evaluated in the future. We formulate this problem as performative signal control under observed traveler responses and characterize performative stability of the coupled policy-demand system. We propose incremental day-to-day retiming using the local policy gradient at the current operating point, estimated offline through simulation-based zeroth-order optimization without an explicit day-to-day demand-response model. This gradual approach provides a feasible path for policy and demand to co-evolve toward stability. Experiments on a downtown Denver network show that our approach improves congestion, throughput, and stability, generalizes across different demand levels, and remains effective when the offline simulator contains mismatched travel demand and routing behaviors.
item.dc:creator: Shuchang Jiang, Xinwu Qian, Santiago Segarra, Zhongyuan Zhao

item.title: Global Parameter Identification and Uncertainty Quantification of reduced-order ADM1 using Maximum Likelihood Estimation and Bayesian Inference
item.description: arXiv:2610.19098v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Anaerobic digestion (AD) models can be challenging to calibrate against real data due to limited practical identifiability, data scarcity, and model complexity. Weighted least squares objective functions and gradient-based solvers using finite differences are often used in literature, but result in suboptimal parameter estimates and large uncertainty bands. This paper identifies the parameters of a reduced-order ADM1 by comparing the frameworks of maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) and Bayesian inference (BI), and quantifies uncertainties of parameters and outputs. Multirate experimental data are taken from a lab-scale AD reactor fed with agricultural substrates and operated at organic loading rates of 3$\,$g VS $\mathrm{m^{-3}d^{-1}}$. Global optima are found via global and gradient-based local search algorithms using forward sensitivities. Enhanced scatter search provides the best global search results. These are refined by the Gauss-Newton algorithm as the best local search, which delivers $R^2$ values of 0.95 for acetic acid and 0.77 for biogas production. BI yields substantially narrower uncertainty bands than MLE and avoids the need for a global search by incorporating prior knowledge about parameter distributions. The search space is captured efficiently by log10 scaling of parameters. Algorithmic details on its implications are provided. Despite a high-resolution lab-scale dataset, the ADM1-specific inhibition parameter $K_\mathrm{I,nh3}$ is practically not identifiable with MLE, and shows a low output sensitivity, whereas a parameter for the effective ion concentration shows superb practical identifiabilty at high confidence with both MLE and BI. The present work lays a scalable base for calibration of nonlinear AD models by providing reliable simulations. It thus advances model-based monitoring and control applications of multirate processes such as agricultural AD plants.
item.dc:creator: Simon Hellmann, Leander Lerch, Terrance Wilms, Moritz Reumsch\"ussel, Alberto Meola, F\'elix Delory, Steffi Knorn, Stefan Streif, S\"oren Weinrich

item.title: Measurements and Analysis of Distortion in Inertial Force Exciters for Flat-Panel Loudspeakers
item.description: arXiv:2610.19125v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Flat-panel loudspeakers are typically driven by dynamic exciters that employ a voice coil coupled to a reaction mass to exert force on the panel. Unlike conventional loudspeakers, where the cone is relatively light weight, heavy panels may require significant exertion from the driver to achieve sound pressure levels required of consumer grade loudspeakers. Overexertion can cause harmonic distortion and reduced sound quality, especially in drivers where the voice coil is not centered in the magnetic field. There are many different exciters available commercially with different power ratings and price points. The frequency response, linearity, total-harmonic distortion (THD), intermodulation distortion (IMD), and force vs. displacement were measured for three types of exciters to determine the consistency of manufacturing and use in panel loudspeakers. These exciters were found to have high variability in all metrics among units of the same type. Distortion metrics such as IMD may be reduced by running impedance sweeps to match exciters with similar response characteristics in multi-actuator panels.
item.dc:creator: Stephen F. Roessner, Michael C. Heilemann

item.title: A Decoupled Approach for Modeling N-k Interdiction with Induced Failures in Electric Power Grids
item.description: arXiv:2610.19289v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The electric power grid is a critical infrastructure system subject to different types of failures which can have devastating impacts on society. One framework to study the resilience of the grid is the N-k interdiction model, which introduces an attacker and defender model to identify grid vulnerabilities. However, traditional N-k interdiction models characterize the power grid with steady-state assumptions. One key aspect missing from this analysis is the behavior of the grid as it evolves from the pre-failure grid state and post-failure grid state. During such a transition period, automated protection systems, transient instabilities, and other phenomena can trigger cascading failures that can occur before grid operators can respond. To bridge this gap, this paper first introduces the generalized induced failure N-k (N-k.k') problem, where an initial set of k failures induces an additional set of k' failures. In this context, we propose a disjoint optimization approach that decouples the computation of cascading failures from the interdiction model. This system response model, furthermore, is treated as a black box module without compromising the underlying performance guarantees of the interdiction model. Extensive experiments on several benchmark power grid case studies showcase the efficacy and scalability of the approach.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Chio, Kaarthik Sundar, Russell Bent, Nalini Venkatasubramanian

item.title: A Critical Review of Grid Integration Challenges and Flexibility Opportunities for Large-Scale Data Centers
item.description: arXiv:2610.19374v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The rapid proliferation of cloud computing and artificial intelligence workloads is fundamentally reshaping the magnitude, spatial concentration, and electrical characteristics of data center power demand. Data centers differ from conventional commercial loads because they combine high rack densities, converter-dominated interfaces, thermally coupled cooling, uninterruptible power supplies, programmable workloads, and increasingly complex behind-the-meter generation and storage within a single facility. This review examines their grid integration from utility and sustainable-energy perspectives across resource planning, large-load interconnection, distribution feeders, market operation, real-time dynamics, power quality, and asset management. Particular attention is given to distribution-level issues that receive limited treatment in broader energy reviews: bidirectional operation on renewable-rich feeders, harmonic propagation and resonance, ride-through and reconnection, transformer derating, cable ampacity, neutral-conductor heating, protection, and measurement. Static, composite, physics-based dynamic, calibrated, impedance, electromagnetic transient, and hybrid load models are compared according to study purpose and data requirements, and utility coordination platforms, uninterruptible power supply and battery control, workload flexibility, renewable co-location, cogeneration, fuel cells, thermal storage, and clean firm supply are assessed. The central finding is that requested peak demand and annual energy matching alone cannot establish reliable or sustainable integration. Credible assessment must consider hourly and locational supply, network deliverability, marginal emissions, lifecycle and water impacts, backup obligations, rebound, asset health, and verified operating capability.
item.dc:creator: Bibek Dhakal, Manohar Chamana, Biswambhar Gayen, Jatendar Kumar, S M Shams Rahman, Aaqib Peerzada, Ki Yeob Lee, Olatunji M. Adeyanju, Bhaskar Mitra, Soumya Kundu, Stephen Bayne

item.title: Multiscale distributed MPC for Optimal Transport
item.description: arXiv:2610.19390v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we present a novel multiscale formulation for the Optimal Transport (OT) of large swarms. The scheme is divided in two levels, a top-level OT formulation with a terminal penalty cost to handle time-varying densities, and a low-level, Model Predictive Controller (MPC) that allows agents to track the nominal velocity under control affine dynamics and rejects external disturbances. We show that the terminal-penalty dynamic formulation reduces to a regularized static dual, which agents solve in a distributed way to compute the nominal velocity.We also prove distributional input-to-state stability in the $1$-Wasserstein metric of the density flow with respect to the mismatch that the low-level and the target motion introduce, so that the tracking error only perturbs the macroscopic flow by a bounded, quantifiable amount. Finally, we demonstrate via simulations the effectiveness of the proposed method handling time-varying targets and state perturbations.
item.dc:creator: Guillem Pascual, Yu-Jen Huang, Sonia Mart\'inez

item.title: Optimistic Distributed Submodular Coordination with Applications to Multi-Target Tracking with Multiple Robots
item.description: arXiv:2610.19417v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide a distributed online algorithm for multi-agent submodular coordination in bandit environments, i.e., environments whose evolution is unknown a priori and may even adapt to the agents' actions. We are motivated by multi-robot tasks such as target tracking, where the optimal actions change over time and the agents must track them rather than a single fixed optimum. To address such problems, we provide the Optimistic Distributed Online Greedy (O-DOG) algorithm, that leverages predictions about the environment's behavior and improves regret guarantees. The agents select actions simultaneously over arbitrary, possibly time-varying, network topologies, and each agent acts optimistically, i.e., leveraging predictions of its upcoming rewards, e.g., from forecasts of the targets' motion and of its neighbors' actions. We bound O-DOG's tracking regret in terms of the agents' prediction error and the bound never exceeds its prediction-free counterpart. Particularly, it is sublinear even when the optimal action changes at every time step, provided the predictions are accurate enough. We further quantify the suboptimality due to decentralization as a function of the network structure, and show that accurate predictions accelerate convergence. We validate O-DOG in simulated multi-robot target tracking.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Sharma, Atharva Navsalkar, Zirui Xu, Vasileios Tzoumas

item.title: Traffic State Prediction and Control Using a Koopman Operator Framework with Polynomial Observables
item.description: arXiv:2610.19442v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we develop a Koopman operator framework for modeling and control of traffic flow governed by the Lighthill--Whitham--Richards (LWR) conservation law. We show that the nonlinear dynamics induced by the Greenshields flow--density relation naturally motivate a dictionary of polynomial observables, while the controlled dynamics become bilinear in the lifted Koopman coordinates. A reduced-order Koopman model is identified from spatio-temporal traffic-density snapshots and used as the prediction model in a model predictive control (MPC) framework for ramp metering. The resulting Koopman-MPC is compared with two predictive control baselines that use, respectively, a fixed linearized LWR model and the nonlinear finite-volume LWR model. In a one-hour freeway experiment, the Koopman-based controller maintains the traffic density below the critical Greenshields value and closely reproduces the behavior of the nonlinear PDE-based MPC, with a maximum-density difference below 1%. The Koopman predictor also reduces the mean online model-evaluation cost by approximately one order of magnitude relative to the nonlinear PDE predictor. In contrast, the linearized LWR predictor is computationally cheaper but exhibits substantially larger prediction errors and yields a more conservative metering policy. These results demonstrate that the analytical structure of the nonlinear traffic conservation law can be exploited to construct an interpretable data-driven surrogate for efficient traffic prediction and control
item.dc:creator: Shakib Mustavee, Arvind Singh, Shaurya Agarwal

item.title: Heterogeneous Services in Multi-UAV Networks with No-Fly Zone and User Mobility
item.description: arXiv:2610.19515v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we investigate a wireless communication network supported by multiple uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs). To ensure reliable connectivity, UAVs are desired to approach the boundaries of designated no-fly zones (NFZs) without violating them when mobile users (MUs) enter NFZs. To support heterogeneous communication services, MUs are assigned different priority levels based on their individual communication types. Considering the practical constraints arising from user mobility, heterogeneous communication requirements, and NFZs, the objective is to maximize the weighted sum of MU communication rates, where weights correspond to MU priorities. This is achieved by jointly optimizing trajectory planning, UAV transmission power control, and the binary association factor between UAVs and MUs. To address this challenging optimization problem under dynamic constraints, we develop a soft actor-critic algorithm with prioritized experience replay, which learns an adaptive control policy. Numerical results show that the proposed algorithm outperforms benchmark schemes in terms of convergence speed and stability. Moreover, it effectively meets diverse communication requirements, satisfies UAV energy constraints, and ensures reliable operation under NFZ constraints.
item.dc:creator: Bin Li, Senning Wan, Decheng Zhang, Yonglei Yao, Yu Xue

item.title: Identifiability-Guided Composite Load Modeling of AI Data Centers
item.description: arXiv:2610.19565v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The rapid growth of AI data centers introduces large, workload-dependent loads whose protection and reconnection behavior can affect power-system transient stability. Calibrating dynamic models of such loads is challenging because treating all associated elements as freely estimable may lead to weakly identified or physically confounded parameterizations. This paper proposes an identifiability-guided calibration framework for a composite load model with separate IT, cooling, and auxiliary branches. A nuisance-projected Fisher-information criterion characterizes the local identifiability of the cooling-motor composition, while a workload non-equivalence result shows that voltage-only recalibration cannot reproduce workload-dependent responses. Guided by these results, a grey-box estimator trained with branch-level supervision learns the workload-to-power relation and the cooling composition, while retaining a prescribed UPS protection law and an externally anchored reconnect-ramp duration. The learned workload relation is then distilled into a closed form for transient-stability simulation. Evaluation using 300,000 MIT Supercloud GPU power-utilization samples and 12,600 IEEE 39-bus fault scenarios yields an aggregate active-power $R^2$ of 0.948, compared with 0.856 for an LSTM baseline. Removing branch-level supervision preserves relatively high aggregate accuracy but substantially degrades cooling-component recovery. Under unseen deep voltage sags, the proposed model achieves a transient $R^2$ of 0.750, compared with 0.033 for the LSTM. Closed-loop simulations further show that cooling composition and protection behavior can affect retained-load states and voltage responses near protection thresholds.
item.dc:creator: Ding Lin, Jianhui Wang, Meng Yue, Tianqiao Zhao

item.title: Severity-Aware Minimum Security Sets for Accelerated Preventive SCOPF Using Machine Learning
item.description: arXiv:2610.19750v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proposes a severity-aware machine learning framework for reducing the computational burden of preventive AC security-constrained optimal power flow (PSCOPF). The central idea is to identify a compact minimum security set (MSS) containing only the non-dominated contingencies and associated post-contingency constraints that materially influence the preventive operating point while satisfying a prescribed severity tolerance. An offline procedure combines AC security assessment, severity-based ranking, non-dominated screening, and iterative reduced PSCOPF. After each reduced PSCOPF solution, exhaustive security assessment over all credible contingencies identifies additional contingency--constraint pairs whose residual severity exceeds the specified threshold. Severity is characterized using the normalized number, accumulated magnitude, maximum magnitude, and average magnitude of post-contingency violations. The resulting operating-point-dependent MSSs are used as labels for a supervised multi-label learning model that predicts the security elements required to construct the reduced PSCOPF directly from the pre-contingency state. The proposed framework therefore focuses the optimization on the contingencies and constraints that affect preventive control decisions, reducing problem size and computation time while explicitly controlling residual post-contingency severity. Results on the IEEE 60-bus and 118-bus systems, the latter having an approximately seven-times-larger PSCOPF formulation, demonstrate substantial computational reductions with limited impact on the preventive operating solution.
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Iman Alizadeh, Saeed Zeynali, Salah Ghamizi, Sylvain Kubler

item.title: Iteratively Convex Frequency Data-Driven Synthesis of Structured MIMO Controllers
item.description: arXiv:2610.19756v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Frequency-response-function-based controller design enables synthesis directly from measured data, avoiding the need for accurate parametric plant models. This paper presents a generalized IQC-based approach for convex synthesis of structured MIMO feedback and feedforward controllers from frequency response function data. The framework supports flexible controller parametrizations, multiple performance objectives, and both singular-value and element-wise performance shaping of MIMO controllers within a unified frequency-domain formulation. To facilitate practical deployment, the synthesis approach is embedded within a bootstrapped controller design methodology that progressively increases controller flexibility while refining the performance specifications. The resulting approach is validated experimentally on the motion stage of an industrial wirebonder, where clear performance improvement is demonstrated through MIMO $\mathcal{H}_\infty$ synthesis, element-wise feedback shaping, and dynamic feedforward design. The results demonstrate that high-performance multivariable controllers can be synthesized directly from measured FRF data in a practical and systematic manner.
item.dc:creator: Luuk Marceau Spin, Thom Samuels, Dragan Kostic, Maurice W. P. M. H. Heemels, Nathan van de Wouw, Roland Toth

item.title: Resilient Angle-Constrained Formation Control and Localization Under DoS Attacks (Extended Version)
item.description: arXiv:2610.19824v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies resilient angle-constrained leader--follower formation control and localization of multi-agent systems under asynchronous denial-of-service (DoS) attacks, which block individual sensing and communication links. To preserve the well-posedness of angle-based localization, an all-or-nothing triangle integrity protocol (ANTIP) is proposed to convert edge-wise attacks into triangle-wise ones, and DoS attacks are classified into localizability-maintained and localizability-broken attacks. First, with relative position measurements over attack-free links, resilient formation tracking laws are designed for leaders with constant velocities and with time-varying velocities comprising translational, rotational, and scaling motions. These laws guarantee asymptotic tracking and finite-time recovery of tracking, respectively, when the duration of localizability-broken attacks is suitably bounded. Second, with only angle measurements and communications, a resilient simultaneous localization and formation control (RSLAF) scheme is developed. It combines a finite-time distributed observer, which estimates the exosystem matrices and states under asynchronous DoS attacks, with a perturbation-based localization law that prevents localization from getting stuck at degenerate configurations. The theoretical results are rigorously proved and illustrated by numerical simulations.
item.dc:creator: Nhat-Minh Le-Phan, Ziliang Lyu, Lihua Xie

item.title: Actuation-Aware Pinching-Antenna Placement Under Blockage and User Mobility
item.description: arXiv:2610.19859v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Existing placement studies for pinching-antenna systems (PASS) usually assume that antenna movement is instantaneous and free. In practice, actuators move at finite speeds and must pause radiation while repositioning. This makes performance depend on consecutive antenna positions, turning placement into an edge-weighted longest-path problem on a temporal trellis. We also show that an obstacle blocks a wider range of antenna positions as it approaches the user, causing sudden performance drops that make multi-step lookahead essential, and that once obstacle height is included every blockage event shadows at least a fixed minimum length of waveguide. We give an exact offline solution with complexity O(TMS) and bound the per-slot loss of a W-step receding-horizon policy by O(1/W). Measurements show that the required lookahead window is set by shadow width rather than by waveguide length. Across 20 random seeds, the exact policy delivers 17.7% higher max-min throughput than per-slot optimization under blockage, and matches it when no blockers are present.
item.dc:creator: Javad Bagherivand

item.title: On the Mechanism of Multi-Cluster System Separation Under Extreme Events
item.description: arXiv:2610.19918v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Historical blackout events demonstrate that, under complex multi-event contingencies, interconnected power systems can split into multiple areas exhibiting distinct dynamic behavior while remaining physically connected. This work provides a rationale for this phenomenon. Typical N-1 contingency analysis leads to a response dominated by a single unstable mode, supporting the two-cluster conjecture used by transient stability assessment tools such as the SIME method. However, extreme events, often involving cascading N-k contingencies, can excite multiple unstable modes. We establish a proof of concept based on linear modal expansion to show how such concurrent excitation leads to multiple coherent areas. The resulting behavior is illustrated through simulations on the standard WSCC 9-bus, IEEE 14-bus, and IEEE 39-bus systems, demonstrating the limitations of conventional two-cluster representations under extreme events.
item.dc:creator: Nikolaos Sofos, Georgios Tzounas, Federico Milano

item.title: Topology-adaptive Estimation of Maximum Voltage Unbalance for Distribution Networks with Finite-sample Guarantee
item.description: arXiv:2610.20036v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High penetration of single-phase distributed power production and frequent topology changes can significantly increase voltage unbalance in distribution networks. Reliable probabilistic power flow (PPF) assessment for the network, therefore, must account for topology-dependent power-flow equations, numerical error in the voltage unbalance factor (VUF), and finite-sample uncertainty in power measurements. In this paper, we propose Topology-Adaptive Certified Quantile Estimation (TACQE) to estimate the maximum VUF across monitored electric buses. Following a local network change, TACQE updates the cross-couplings among power-flow sequences, and certifies candidate PPF solutions against the updated nonlinear equations. The resulted power-flow state enclosures provide rigorous bounds on the maximum VUF. Furthermore, we derive independent reference-solver evaluations to calibrate discrepancies from the reference PPF solution. This leads to a uniform sampling bound that yields simultaneous upper-tail probabilities and quantiles, which provides a finite-sample guarantee for the estimated maximum-VUF distribution over an entire range of VUF thresholds. From our numerical simulations across 101 fixed-topology quantiles, it demonstrates that the designed TACQE can provide a fast candidate post-change power flow solution where it reuses most of the previous network model and modifies only the affected bus blocks.
item.dc:creator: Jinbao Wang, Jun Liu, Shiliang Zhang, Xuehui Ma, He Zhang

item.title: The Cost of Executability: Temporal Margins for Continuous-Time Multi-Agent Path Finding under Closed-Loop Control
item.description: arXiv:2610.20118v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-agent path finding (MAPF) solvers are evaluated on the schedules they produce, not on how well those schedules can be executed. Specifically, continuous-time optimal solvers can achieve even lower cost than their discrete counterparts by scheduling agents with near-zero temporal/spatial separation, and by exploiting graphs with higher connectedness; however, such schedules may prove hard to execute under a realistic controller. We integrate AOC-CBS, an anytime-optimal continuous-time MAPF solver, into a fleet coordination framework in which each agent tracks its timed path using model predictive control, and we evaluate the resulting system on congested MovingAI benchmark instances with 21 to 40 agents. Without intervention, only a fraction of the instances complete execution. We then apply T-robustness by adding a time-margin, i.e., a minimum temporal gap between agents at shared locations, as well as spatial inflation of the agent footprint. Increasing either margin raises execution success, for a relatively small increase in the schedule's sum-of-costs; it also improves how closely agents adhere to the schedule: when tracking each agent's position throughout execution and comparing it against the position it should occupy according to the schedule, the mean discrepancy falls significantly as the margin increases. In general, the two margins have different effects; temporal margin decreases deviation, giving the controller room to stay on schedule. Spatial margin affects deviation less and instead increases the clearance between agents, so that the same deviation no longer leads to a blocking stall. They are nonetheless substitutes rather than complements: spatial inflation is almost free in schedule cost, but its effect on execution success is small and does not compound with a temporal margin already in place.
item.dc:creator: Sabino Roselli, Alvin Combrink, Ze Zhang

item.title: Robust Data-Driven Controller Synthesis from Sampled and Uncertain Frequency Response Estimates using Integral Quadratic Constraints
item.description: arXiv:2610.20248v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we develop a novel MIMO controller synthesis method that relies solely on frequency-domain data of discrete-time systems. The approach is based on an iterative design procedure using \emph{integral quadratic constraints} (IQCs). It generalizes existing data-driven methods that approximate semi-infinite IQC conditions by enforcing them on a finite set of measured frequency points. Such approximations do not provide guarantees on the continuous frequency axis and may fail to capture inter-frequency behavior. We address this limitation by formulating a convex optimization problem that preserves robustness guarantees over the entire frequency range. In particular, the proposed method explicitly accounts for inter-frequency behavior of both plant and controller, leading to certified robust stability and performance. The effectiveness and computational efficiency of the approach are demonstrated using experimentally obtained frequency response data from industrial-grade semiconductor equipment. The synthesized controller is implemented on the physical setup, and its performance is validated in real-time experiments.
item.dc:creator: Luuk Marceau Spin, Maurice W. P. M. H. Heemels, Nathan van de Wouw, Roland Toth

item.title: Asynchronous Distributed Multi-Sensor Fusion Over Sensor Track Hypotheses
item.description: arXiv:2610.20290v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work proposes a multi-target tracking solution that reasons over combinations of sensor-level tracks to perform distributed multiple hypothesis tracking (MHT) in an asynchronous multi-sensor network. This approach handles clustered target tracking and allows for efficient information pedigree summarization for distributed data fusion (DDF). By decomposing the association problem into partitioned hypothesis sets and fusing across sensor track combinations, the method reduces combinatorial complexity compared to traditional MHT approaches. Evaluation on a satellite constellation-based tracking scenario demonstrates improved estimation accuracy and data association quality compared to a reference target tracker with global nearest neighbor association.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Draves, Nisar Ahmed, Eric Borcherding, Jonathan Chan

item.title: Delay-Enabled Adaptive Learning of Time-Varying Parameters
item.description: arXiv:2610.20322v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proposes a novel adaptive learning method for unknown time-varying parameters by deliberately incorporating a delay into the parameter update. Specifically, a conventional adaptive estimator is augmented with only one additional dynamic state, which estimates the parameter variation rate from the difference between current and previous parameter estimates. The method fundamentally changes the influence of time variation on estimation performance: the resulting estimation error is governed by the second derivative of the unknown parameter rather than its first derivative. Under persistent excitation, a small-gain analysis proves exponential stability of the complete estimation-error system and establishes explicit bounds for the parameter, state-prediction, and parameter-rate errors. In particular, accurate learning of linearly time-varying parameters and their unknown rates can be guaranteed with errors converging exponentially fast to zero. Numerical comparisons with conventional adaptive estimation and a recent timevarying parameter estimator demonstrate superior learning performance in the considered examples. The proposed delay-enabled adaptive estimator requires neither state derivatives nor any assumed model of parameter variation, and its implementation consists of one delayed difference and a first-order filter. These results thus provide a direct extension of adaptive learning from constant to time-varying parameters without sacrificing the simplicity of the conventional adaptive estimation mechanism.
item.dc:creator: Chengzhi Yuan, Mingxi Zhou

item.title: A Practical Framework for Incremental Testing and Technology Maturation of Spacecraft Autonomy
item.description: arXiv:2610.20433v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper addresses the "trust gap" in deploying AI-enabled spacecraft autonomy through an integrated verification framework combining offline ground testing with online flight monitoring. The offline phase progresses systematically through simulation studies, processor-in-the-loop (PIL), hardware-in-the-loop (HIL), and robotic emulation testing, culminating in flight validation. The online phase employs AI watchdog systems for performance monitoring and safety guardrails for real-time constraint enforcement. Key contributions include: (1) systematic organization of verification techniques emphasizing closed-loop behavioral testing at each phase, (2) integration of AI watchdogs with runtime assurance, and (3) demonstration of the framework through a reinforcement learning-based attitude control case study. This approach integrates mature technologies to provide a viable pathway for safe deployment of AI-enabled autonomy in high-consequence space operations while addressing simulation-to-reality transfer challenges.
item.dc:creator: Kerianne Hobbs, Ben Bycroft, Pamela Wood, Mathew W. Bissonnette, M. J. Durst, Kimberly Sover, Alexandra Mangel, Gabriel Behrendt, Upneet Singh, Juan Rodriguez, Lukas Dillingham, Zeve Akerling, Nicholas Oune, Daniel Thomlinson, Evan N. Sperber, Denise Burrell, Phaedrus Leeds, Brian Hardy, Nathaniel Hamilton, Raul Santos, Arturo de la Barcena, Kyle Dunlap

item.title: Controller- and Communication-Aware Flexibility Margins for Electric Distribution Networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.20484v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops a framework for quantifying operational flexibility in radial electric distribution systems under coupled active- and reactive-load uncertainty. Flexibility is defined as the largest scaling of a prescribed uncertainty set that can be accommodated while satisfying network and actuator limits under a given control architecture. We consider a one-sided Euclidean set for robust demand-growth capability, with a direct extension to bidirectional variations. Under LinDistFlow, controllable distributed resources and feeder-head exchange with the upstream grid jointly balance active-power disturbances, while local Volt/VAR feedback regulates reactive power. The resulting affine closed-loop disturbance response admits exact second-order-cone robust counterparts. For fixed Volt/VAR gains, a convex reformulation jointly optimizes the flexibility margin and active-power participation factors, including feeder-head participation. A sparse load-to-generator feedforward map further captures communication constraints. Numerical studies on the Iowa-240 feeder demonstrate how the amount of control authority and communication structure shape the achievable flexibility margin.
item.dc:creator: Saif R. Kazi, Kaarthik Sundar

item.title: FedRIC: Heterogeneity-Aware Federated Learning with Hard Deadline Constraints in Open RAN
item.description: arXiv:2610.20530v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Open Radio Access Networks (O-RANs) bring intelligence to disaggregated RANs through virtualized platforms and open interfaces, but the stringent latency budgets of the RAN Intelligent Controller (RIC) and heterogeneous traffic conditions make real-time deployment costly. Centralized learning is ill-suited to the RIC due to its computational burden, timing constraints, and communication overhead, motivating Federated Learning (FL) as a distributed alternative. We formulate FL in O-RAN as a Mixed-Integer Nonlinear Program (MINLP) that minimizes communication cost and learning time under heterogeneity in User Equipment (UE) compute, traffic, and channel conditions, and decompose it into a UE Assignment (UA) subproblem and a Computation and Bandwidth Allocation (CBA) subproblem. We then propose FedRIC, a heterogeneity-aware FL framework combining compressed gradient descent, slice-aware resource allocation, and multilevel hierarchical aggregation. Experiments show that FedRIC outperforms FedCOM, FedAvg, and QFedAvg in convergence rate, communication cost, and latency.
item.dc:creator: Adhwaa Al-Chaab, Ayman Younis, Dario Pompili

item.title: CIPHEUR: LLM-Guided Structural Search Control for Conflict-Graph Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2610.16158v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Conflict-graph search can stagnate despite effective operators when interventions fail to address the conflicts blocking progress. A disruptive intervention may also require further search before its value emerges. We propose CIPHEUR, a large language model (LLM)-guided framework that connects conflict evidence to coordinated intervention and recovery through Structured Intervention Units (SIUs). The shared control interface supports offline synthesis of executable policies and online contextual decisions. Asynchronous online control sustains native search during inference, while all policies preserve the original objective and feasibility constraints. Across eight satellite-ground scheduling conflict views with five runs per view and a 900-second evaluation cap, CIPHEUR-online achieves the highest mean objective among 11 configurations and increases mean scheduled contact duration by 14.84% over the greedy baseline GWMIN. It exceeds the strongest external per-view mean in seven of eight views and outperforms CHILS in all 40 paired runs. Within the same runs, its normalized objective improvement from 360 to 900 seconds is 1.50 to 1.86 times that of the two programmatic controllers. A separately frozen, one-shot LLM-generated controller also improves the mean objective over CHILS without runtime model calls. Together, these results demonstrate how structural search control translates LLM design knowledge and contextual reasoning into improved solution quality and sustained search progress.
item.dc:creator: Yuqing Cheng, Yan Jia, Yanjie Song, Xiaolu Liu, Lining Xing, Feng Yao

item.title: DiffGIPC: Differentiable Mixed-Coordinate Contact Dynamics on GPU
item.description: arXiv:2610.19091v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Contact-rich inverse problems require efficient gradients and reliable enforcement of non-penetration. Existing differentiable methods provide fast simulation and rigid-deformable coupling, but contact treatments based on penalties or velocity-level constraints can permit penetration or positional drift. Incremental Potential Contact (IPC) maintains non-penetration through geometric barriers and {continuous collision detection (CCD)}. However, repeated forward and backward evaluations remain costly in full-space finite-element (FEM) implementations, particularly when nearly rigid components retain many vertex {degrees of freedom (DoFs)}. We present DiffGIPC, a GPU-accelerated differentiable IPC framework for optimizing interacting deformable and nearly rigid bodies. Our affine-body derivatives enable {rest-shape} design, initial-state optimization, and articulated control while retaining only twelve motion DoFs per affine body. These gradients account for how changes in geometry, placement, and actuation affect other objects through collision and friction. We preserve these interactions in one coupled FEM-affine adjoint system per frame, reducing the backward-system size without discarding the dependencies that drive the inverse problem. GPU-optimized backward computation further reduces the cost of repeated gradient evaluations. A reusable PyTorch interface connects supported physical parameters to user-defined parameter maps and losses across design, identification, motion, placement, and articulated control. Experiments demonstrate peak speedups over DiffIPC of approximately 150.0x with full-space FEM and 4133.3x with affine bodies for combined forward simulation and backward differentiation.
item.dc:creator: Kemeng Huang, Bowen Ren, Xinyu Lu, Minchen Li, Taku komura

item.title: Learning in Orbit: Onboard Training and Closed-Loop Attitude Control with a Thermal Segmentation Model on a Spacecraft
item.description: arXiv:2610.19122v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deep space missions increasingly require spacecraft capable of autonomously operating in environments with communication delays and bandwidth limitations. A key enabler of such autonomy is the ability to run learning-based algorithms directly onboard. In this work, we present a flight deployment on a 6U CubeSat that demonstrates (1) onboard training and inference of a thermal segmentation model on an NVIDIA Jetson TX2 NX GPU in space and (2) closed-loop attitude control using the segmentation model on a real-time, thermal image feed to track the Moon. In addition to this demonstration, we implement ROS 2 Foxy as a data transport middleware and integrate an open-source file system that provides strong data integrity guarantees and self-healing features. Over the course of approximately one year, we performed 12 experiments on the spacecraft, advancing the state of the art in autonomous spacecraft systems by showing how modern learning-based pipelines, commercially available hardware, and open-source software can operate reliably under the compute and environmental constraints of Low Earth Orbit (LEO).
item.dc:creator: Elena Sorina Lupu, Hannah Grauer, Phaedrus Leeds, Nikhil Ranganathan, Connor Lee, Sulekha Kishore, Cailyn Smith, Shon Cortes, Brian Hardy, Benjamen Bycroft, Darren W. Rowen, Soon-Jo Chung

item.title: Full-Order Safety for Nonlinear Reduced-Order MPC
item.description: arXiv:2610.19250v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reduced-order models (ROMs) make model predictive control (MPC) of high-dimensional nonlinear systems tractable, but the resulting modeling error can lead to constraint violations on the real system. We introduce CoRE-MPC, a robust MPC formulation that plans with a nonlinear ROM and guarantees recursive feasibility and constraint satisfaction for the full-order system. It can be applied with a broad class of nonlinear model reduction techniques and the resulting MPC does not require evaluating the full-order model online, thus ensuring computational efficiency. The key insight is in how the ROM affects the dynamics of the prediction error. We account for this with two error radii that are propagated alongside the ROM and provide a guaranteed bound on the prediction error. The approach is validated in simulation on an 80-state oscillator chain, a Burgers equation, and a 9,768-state finite-element soft robot, where a two-state ROM with data-driven bounds keeps all 1,628 nodes clear of a wall at a median solve time below 1 ms for a 20 ms control period. Across these examples, CoRE-MPC is 13 to 61 times faster than full-order robust MPC at only 27 to 35% higher closed-loop cost, whereas existing certified schemes are either infeasible or at least twice as conservative. Code: [released upon publication].
item.dc:creator: Luis Pabon, Johannes K\"{o}hler, Revant Kasichainula, Marco Pavone

item.title: Comprehensive Comparisons of Reinforcement Learning Algorithms in Autonomous Driving
item.description: arXiv:2610.19429v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive comparison of four representative reinforcement learning (RL) methods in autonomous vehicle (AV) decision-making, including: Fitted Value Iteration (FVI), Rollout Classification Policy Iteration (RCPI), Deep Q-Network (DQN), and a discrete-action adaptation of Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (D-DDPG). The four methods are applied to the same AV decision-making problem at an unsignalized intersection and are compared in terms of optimality and safety, training stability, and training and decision cost. RCPI is the closest to a reference solution and has the most stable training process. However, it is the least data-efficient. D-DDPG reaches the second-smallest gap to a reference solution with the highest data efficiency, but has the least training stability. DQN is the most stable model-free method but has the highest collision rate. FVI achieves a lower collision rate than DQN, but is less data-efficient and less stable. Based on these results, we provide suggestions for selecting a method according to whether a model is available, the budget for training, and whether stable training is required.
item.dc:creator: Dechen Xie, Mushuang Liu

item.title: Runtime Monitoring of Supermartingale Certificates
item.description: arXiv:2610.19701v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Supermartingale certificates formally guarantee temporal properties of discrete and continuous-time stochastic dynamical systems. However, these guarantees rely on a mathematical model of the world, leaving a sim-to-real gap that can invalidate them for the deployed system. We formulate the runtime monitoring problem for supermartingale certificates, in which a monitor observes a single system trajectory and raises an alarm when there is sufficient statistical evidence that the supermartingale certificate has been violated during execution. We present an algorithm to automatically construct a monitor using betting-based sequential tests that bound the probability of ever raising a false alarm at a user-specified level. Within this betting framework, we formulate strategies that allow the monitor to exploit spatial regularity to improve detection power while preserving this statistical guarantee. We demonstrate the efficacy of our approach on supermartingale certificate benchmarks from the literature.
item.dc:creator: Mirco Giacobbe, Thomas A. Henzinger, Konstantin Kueffner, Emily Yu, \DJ{}or\dj{}e \v{Z}ikeli\'{c}

item.title: Mixed-Reality Feedback Control: Towards Blending of Control and Digital Twinning
item.description: arXiv:2610.19759v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Technologies, such as co-simulation, in particular, digital twins (DTs) are used for comprehensive and reliable prototyping, verification and validation (V&V) of control systems. There, the combination of feedback loops across multiple realities (e.g., simulations, physical setups) enables various forms of experimentation with robots and autonomous systems. However, the handling of multiple realities requires a more specific support by the modelling techniques used in control engineering. To streamline the latter in the system life cycle, we propose a framework for mixing (i.e., fusing, defusing) control input and feedback signals (i.e., stimuli, responses) in simultaneously operated plants for multiple realities.
item.dc:creator: Melisa Soydan, Mario Gleirscher

item.title: L1 Minimum Energy Estimation of Positive Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.19976v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a novel class of minimum energy estimation problems for positive linear systems with linear costs subject to coupled process and measurement disturbances, where the latter is bounded by the state and the former is bounded by the noise. Through dynamic programming we show that the problem admits explicit solutions. Remarkably, the Luenberger observer structure of the optimal estimator emerges from the optimization itself, with a switching gain that inherits the sparsity of the disturbance constraints, and it is obtained from a differential equation in the finite horizon case. In the infinite horizon case, an algebraic equation characterizes the limit of the finite-horizon solution and yields a stationary estimator with a static gain. We introduce two distinct notions of detectability to characterize when the static gain stabilizes the error dynamics while preserving their positivity, and analyze under which conditions the stationary solution can be formulated as a linear program. We further establish that a disturbance perturbation of finite L1-norm yields an estimation error of finite L1-norm. The framework is illustrated on a large-scale irrigation network.
item.dc:creator: Alba Gurpegui Ram\'on

item.title: Ergodic and Metastable Behavior of Stochastic Popularity Dynamics in Social Networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.20021v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper studies popularity dynamics in social networks, where users' engagement with competing channels is driven by intrinsic content quality, social influence, and popularity feedback. We introduce a stochastic model in which users interact through a directed influence network and channel exposure depends jointly on these three mechanisms. We first characterize the resulting dynamics in the absence of intrinsic quality, showing that popularity concentrates asymptotically on a single channel, leading to a winner-takes-all regime. When all channels have positive intrinsic quality, we establish ergodicity of the popularity process and characterize its long-run behavior. We further show that, when intrinsic quality is small, the system exhibits metastable behavior: it can remain for long periods near configurations dominated by a single channel before transitioning to another. These results highlight how weak quality differences can coexist with strong path dependence induced by popularity feedback. We then investigate platform-level interventions and propose controls that compensate for network-induced exposure biases and mitigate excessive concentration. Analytical results are illustrated through numerical simulations and an empirical analysis of YouTube data, whose observed popularity dynamics are consistent with the proposed stochastic framework. The results provide a mathematical framework for understanding the interplay between quality, social influence, and reinforcement in online popularity dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Chiara Ravazzi, Paolo Frasca, Gaya Cocca

item.title: Sequential Learning-Based Physics-Informed Neural Network Modeling for Parameter Estimation on a Power Converter
item.description: arXiv:2610.20041v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A staged physics-informed neural network (PINN) is proposed for identifying the inductance, capacitance and parasitic resistances of a DC buck converter from time-domain data. Gradients are released in the order of L to C to rL to rC, a sequence derived from sensitivity analysis. The five-stage schedule recovers L and C to within 5% and the series ESR to 10%, while a three-stage variant attains the same accuracy 11% faster. An 84 factorial sweep confirms that the trained PINN remains accurate for simultaneous 8% perturbations of all four components, achieving a waveform RMSE of 2.6 x 10-2 over 5 ms-an order-of-magnitude better than a simultaneous-training baseline.
item.dc:creator: Samuela Rokocakau, Panagiotis Kakosimos, Giulia Tresca, Pericle Zanchetta

item.title: Radial-Angular Resolution Framework for Near-Field Communications
item.description: arXiv:2610.20092v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Near-field beamfocusing confines radiated power into a localized three-dimensional focal spot, making the analytical characterization of radial and angular resolution critical for sixth-generation (6G) multi-user systems, yet existing models treat the focal resolution as a fixed geometric outcome rather than a tunable design variable. Based on the Angular Representation (ASR) approach, this paper presents a resolution framework to design contiguous focal regions across both the radial and angular domain for steered multi-user systems. By extending the definition of a tunable inter-beam overlap $\rho$, we derive closed-form expressions for the radial and angular focal boundaries and extents, alongside the steering-dependent minimum focal distance $d_{0,\text{min}}$ and maximum steering angle $\theta_{\text{max}}$. Using these boundaries, iterative synthesis algorithms are developed to construct uniform and non-uniform radial and angular beam arrangements. Finally, by analyzing both isolated and joint radial-angular configurations, we quantify the fundamental trade-offs between $\rho$, achievable user capacity, inter-user interference, and system sum-rate across varying steering angles.
item.dc:creator: Viviana Centritto, Sotiris Droulias, Angeliki Alexiou

item.title: Enabling Tidying Tasks in Robotic Vacuum Cleaners via a Geometry-Induced Self-Locking Deployable Linkage
item.description: arXiv:2610.20150v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Robotic vacuum cleaners must extend their functionality within tight limits on size, cost, and durability. Deployable linkages with few actuators meet these limits, but their backdrivability makes it difficult to hold a load-bearing posture without continuous motor torque. We introduce a two-stage deployable linkage that is self-locking, in the sense used for toggle and singularity-based linkages, through its own geometry: at full deployment an internal three-link subchain approaches a collinear, near-singular configuration where the input--output transmission ratio approaches zero, so that plate loads produce a small residual back-driving torque, absorbed by drive-train friction and a lightweight magnetic detent. A single actuator performs deployment and locking, a passive chassis-mounted trigger releases the lock for retraction, and a second actuator adjusts only the deployment height. We integrate the mechanism into a commercial robotic vacuum cleaner and validate it through a 100-cycle repeatability test, a quasi-static load test in which the locked plate held 50\,N with the motor de-energized, and 140 pushing-type tidying trials on seven household objects against a commercial arm-equipped vacuum robot under a documented protocol. We derive the analytical holding condition and discuss its limits as an intermediate design point between passive compliance and articulated manipulation.
item.dc:creator: Eunseok Song, inwoong Kim, Sohee Lim, Taehyeong Kim, Yongkook Kim, Hyeontaek Lim, Hyungmin Son, Seungyong Hyung

item.title: Adversarial Reinforcement Learning for Robust Planetary Landing
item.description: arXiv:2610.20252v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) policies for planetary landing and other aerospace guidance, navigation, and control tasks are commonly trained under randomized disturbances to improve robustness. However, typical stochastic perturbation sampling assumes independent variations, whereas real mission disturbances often exhibit spatial and temporal correlation and cannot be reproduced through independent random draws. This work investigates adversarial reinforcement learning to discover challenging off-nominal conditions. A secondary agent generates physically constrained perturbations that degrade the performance of a landing controller, forming an asymmetric sequential zero-sum game. Training proceeds in three stages: baseline controller learning, robustness enhancement with stochastic perturbations, and an iterative adversarial phase in which the controller and disturbance generator are alternately optimized. Preliminary experiments in a three-degree-of-freedom landing environment show that adversarial disturbances reveal vulnerabilities missed by conventional randomization and provide early indications that, with a more extensive training campaign, the approach can yield improved robustness and stronger generalization under previously unseen perturbation regimes.
item.dc:creator: Miguel Leiva-V\'elez, Nicolas Gaston-Rozado, Andrea Scorsoglio, Hodei Urrutxua, V\'ictor Rodr\'iguez-Fern\'andez

item.title: VIGOR-MPC: Vision-Guided Objective Regulation MPC
item.description: arXiv:2610.20333v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Controlling an agent in an environment solely perceived through onboard vision is challenging: perception yields noisy, variable-length, and partially occluded context, while onboard compute is shared between perception and control, limiting the planning horizon executable in real time. We propose VIGOR-MPC, a modular student-teacher framework, agnostic to the perception pipeline, which addresses reference tracking across navigation tasks by distilling a privileged, field-of-view-aware long-horizon MPC into a computationally lightweight short-horizon MPC whose cost parameters are determined online from vision. The teacher operates in simulation with full state knowledge and a multi-trajectory formulation that guarantees the agent can stay within its field of view. The student observes only the noisy, occluded context produced by a perception module and learns, via a multi-level recurrent mapping, to infer cost parameters that aim to recover the teacher's behavior despite missing information. We evaluate VIGOR-MPC on vision-based autonomous racing in simulation and on hardware. Using only onboard perception of the track, VIGOR-MPC generalizes to tracks unseen during training and approaches the lap times of the privileged long-horizon teacher while reducing per-step computation by over 90%.
item.dc:creator: Jelena Trisovic, Rahel Rickenbach, Marek Landert, Panagiotis Minos, Melanie N. Zeilinger

item.title: The Physics Is the Network: Fast, Training-Free Neural Emulation
item.description: arXiv:2610.20525v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Neural emulation need not require learning a substitute for known physics. We investigate PolyNets that couple a continuous-time neural representation of polynomial dynamics with a simple recurrent network for discrete-time integration. When the governing coefficients are known, the resulting tensor graph requires no training and preserves the prescribed numerical scheme while enabling efficient hardware execution and parallel simulation. Using the one-dimensional Korteweg-de Vries equation, we compare PolyNet with CPU and GPU finite-difference Runge-Kutta solvers and three trained neural models: a state-map emulator, a physics-informed predictor, and a learned-tendency integrator. Analytical soliton solutions provide a reference for amplitude and phase errors across grid resolutions, 10^6 dispersively scaled time steps, ensembles of up to 10^4 trajectories, and varying initial amplitudes. PolyNet achieves accuracy comparable to the numerical solvers, including at amplitudes outside the learned models' training conditions. It combines this fidelity with high GPU throughput, approximately constant over the tested resolution range, and favorable ensemble scaling.
item.dc:creator: Luka Todorovic, Kaushal Gianchandani, Sai Ravela

item.title: Constrained coalition games for USV swarm confrontation
item.description: arXiv:2504.04475v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper formulates unmanned surface vehicle (USV) swarm confrontation as a constrained coalition game, capturing cooperation within swarms and competition between swarms. Local task costs are aggregated into coalition objectives to account for tradeoffs among target approach, interception, and formation maintenance, subject to individual geographic constraints and supply line limits shared within each swarm. For prescribed formation sizes and task assignments, explicit linear matrix inequalities in the task weights are derived to establish strong monotonicity of the coalition pseudogradient, thereby guaranteeing the existence of a unique Nash equilibrium (NE) whenever the joint feasible set is nonempty. A distributed robust NE seeking strategy is then developed by integrating gradient tracking and action estimation with projected primal-dual dynamics using local information and neighbor communication. Adaptive compensation addresses unknown hydrodynamic parameters and bounded time-varying disturbances. The disturbance compensation gains are adjusted through local error feedback without requiring disturbance measurements, prior knowledge of disturbance bounds, or a prescribed disturbance generation model. Under the derived weight conditions, the stated dynamics and communication assumptions, and suitable gain conditions, the physical states of all USVs are shown to converge asymptotically to the unique feasible NE. Numerical simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.
item.dc:creator: Cheng Yuwen, Jialing Zhou, Meng Luan, Guanghui Wen, Tingwen Huang

item.title: Kalman-Bucy Filtering with Randomized Sensing: Fundamental Limits and Sensor Network Design for Field Estimation
item.description: arXiv:2511.03740v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Stability analysis of the Kalman filter under randomly lost measurements has been widely studied. We revisit this problem in a general continuous-time framework, where both the measurement matrix and noise covariance evolve as random processes, capturing variability in sensing locations. Within this setting, we derive a closed-form upper bound on the expected estimation covariance for continuous-time Kalman filtering. We then apply this framework to spatiotemporal field estimation, where the field is modeled as a Gaussian process observed by randomly located, noisy sensors. Using clarity, introduced in our earlier work as a rescaled form of the differential entropy of a random variable, we establish a lower bound on the expected spatially averaged clarity and show that its steady-state value converges to a grid-independent limit as the grid is refined. This result exposes fundamental performance limits through a composite sensing parameter that jointly captures the effects of the number of sensors, noise level, and measurement frequency. Simulations show close agreement between the continuous-time analytical solution and the discrete-time covariance, with the agreement improving as the sampling interval decreases. The analytical solution also avoids the recursive computations required in the discrete-time formulation. Most importantly, the derived limits provide principled and efficient guidelines for sensor network design prior to deployment.
item.dc:creator: Xinyi Wang, Devansh R. Agrawal, Dimitra Panagou

item.title: Bang-Bang Evasion: Its Stochastic Optimality and a Terminal-Set-Based Implementation
item.description: arXiv:2511.21633v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We address the problem of optimal evasion in a planar endgame engagement, where a target with bounded lateral acceleration seeks to avoid interception by a missile guided by a linear feedback law. Contrary to existing approaches, that assume perfect information or use heuristic maneuver models in stochastic settings, we formulate the problem in an inherently stochastic framework involving imperfect information and bounded controls. Complying with the generalized separation theorem, the control law factors in the posterior distribution of the state. We extend the well-known optimality of bang-bang evasion maneuvers in deterministic settings to the realm of realistic, stochastic evasion scenarios. First, we prove that an optimal evasion strategy always exists, and that the set of optimal solutions includes at least one bang-bang policy, rendering the resulting optimal control problem finite-dimensional. Second, leveraging this structure, we propose the closed-loop terminal-set-based evasion (TSE) strategy, and demonstrate its effectiveness in simulation against a proportional navigation pursuer. Monte Carlo simulations show that the TSE strategy outperforms traditional stochastic evasion strategies based on random telegraph, Singer, and weaving models.
item.dc:creator: Liraz Mudrik, Yaakov Oshman

item.title: Verification and Forward Invariance of Control Barrier Functions for Differential-Algebraic Systems
item.description: arXiv:2603.13509v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Differential-algebraic equations (DAEs) arise in power networks, chemical processes, and multibody systems, where algebraic constraints encode physical conservation laws. The safety of such systems is critical, yet safe control is challenging because algebraic constraints restrict allowable state trajectories. Control barrier functions (CBFs) provide computationally efficient safety filters for ordinary differential equation (ODE) systems. However, existing CBF methods are not directly applicable to DAEs due to potential conflicts between the CBF condition and the constraint manifold. This paper introduces DAE-aware CBFs that incorporate the differential-algebraic structure through projected vector fields. We derive conditions that ensure forward invariance of safe sets while preserving algebraic constraints and extend the framework to higher-index DAEs. A systematic verification framework is developed, establishing necessary and sufficient conditions for geometric correctness and feasibility of DAE-aware CBFs. For polynomial systems, sum-of-squares certificates are provided, while for nonpolynomial and neural network candidates, satisfiability modulo theories are used for falsification. The approach is validated on wind turbine and flexible-link manipulator systems.
item.dc:creator: Hongchao Zhang, Mohamad H. Kazma, Meiyi Ma, Taylor T. Johnson, Ahmad F. Taha

item.title: Distributed Optimization with Nesterov Momentum and Finite-Time Quantized Consensus
item.description: arXiv:2604.16906v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In modern large-scale networked systems, rapidly solving optimization problems while utilizing communication resources efficiently is critical for addressing complex tasks. In this paper, we consider an unconstrained distributed optimization problem in which information exchange among nodes is governed by a directed communication graph. In our setup we focus on two key challenges. The first is the zigzag phenomenon caused by the objective functions of individual nodes having significantly different curvature along different directions. The second is that the communication channels among nodes are subject to limited bandwidth, which motivates the use of compressed (quantized) messages. To address both challenges simultaneously, we propose QANM, a distributed optimization algorithm that combines Nesterov momentum with a distributed finite-time quantized consensus protocol. Under strong convexity and smoothness assumptions, we show that our proposed algorithm converges linearly to a neighborhood of the optimal solution. Finally, we evaluate QANM on a distributed sensor-fusion problem. With each method's step size tuned separately, QANM exhibits the fastest initial error reduction among the tested methods, including QAGD, Acc-DNGD-SC, and MSDA. Comparisons with QAGD under the same quantized averaging framework illustrate the empirical benefit of momentum, while experiments at two quantization levels demonstrate quantization-dependent error floors.
item.dc:creator: Ruochen Wu, Xu Du, Karl H. Johansson, Apostolos I. Rikos

item.title: Bearing-based Circumnavigation with Collision Avoidance in Time-varying Graphs under Limited Target Information
item.description: arXiv:2606.27719v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study distributed circumnavigation of a stationary target by a heterogeneous team of agents. Each agent is modelled as a disk rather than a point mass to account for its physical dimensions. The target location is assumed to be accessible only to a small subset of agents, called leaders. The rest, called followers, therefore use only local information available from their designated out-neighbour in the interaction graph characterised by the selection of nearest neighbours. By controlling only angular speeds, we develop a distributed guidance law to circumnavigate a stationary target. The proposed guidance law works for both static and time-varying interaction graphs. Inter-agent collision avoidance is enforced through a logarithmic Barrier Lyapunov (BLF) Function, which guarantees forward invariance of the collision-free set. We show that every follower converges to circumnavigation about the same target as the leader at the end of its directed path in the interaction graph, provided the initial conditions are admissible. Numerical simulations illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method for both static and time-varying topologies.
item.dc:creator: Kushal Pratap Singh, Twinkle Tripathy, Anoop Jain

item.title: Probe Sets for Nonlinear Kalman Filtering: Multi-Center Gains and Covariance Recalibration
item.description: arXiv:2609.14271v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Kalman filters (KFs) choose the gain as the product of the state-measurement cross-covariance and the inverse of the innovation covariance. In nonlinear systems, the predictive distribution generally changes shape, and these covariances require approximation. Conventional nonlinear KFs approximate them around a single center, the predicted state. They can produce inaccurate gains and overconfident covariance estimates when one local approximation does not represent the measurement geometry across the uncertainty region. To address this issue, we introduce probe sets, small covariance-scaled collections of states at which the filter repeats its local approximation. We then select the gain that minimizes the average covariance reported by these local approximations. The same construction is used in our previously proposed covariance recalibration step to improve covariance consistency. The construction applies to different KF variants without requiring a specific approximation rule. For quadratic measurements, we derive conditions under which probing yields lower normalized true error variance than the corresponding single-center gain when prediction uncertainty is sufficiently understated. We apply the framework to four KF variants and compare the resulting filters with multiple baselines across 300 randomized setups for each of two systems. The results show that probing preserves typical accuracy while substantially reducing covariance inconsistency and the rare large-error trajectories that dominate the root mean square of per-run errors. The code is available at https://github.com/Shida-Jiang/Probe_KF.
item.dc:creator: Shida Jiang, Shengyu Tao, Scott Moura

item.title: On composition and decomposition operations for vector spaces, graphs and matroids
item.description: arXiv:2305.16354v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we study the ideas of composition and decomposition in the context of vector spaces, graphs and matroids. For vector spaces $\V_{AB},$ treated as collection of row vectors, with specified column set $A\uplus B,$ we define $\V_{SP}\lrarv \V_{PQ}, S\cap Q= \emptyset, $ to be the collection of all vectors $(f_S,f_Q)$ such that $(f_S,f_P)\in \V_{SP}, (f_P,f_Q)\in \V_{PQ}$. An analogous operation $\G_{SP}\lrarg \G_{PQ}\equivd \G_{PQ}$ can be defined in relation to graphs $\G_{SP}, \G_{PQ},$ on edge sets $S\uplus P, P\uplus Q,$ respectively in terms of an overlapping subgraph $\G_P$ which gets deleted in the right side graph (see for instance the notion of $k-sum$ \cite{oxley}). For matroids we define the `linking' $\M_{SP}\lrarm \M_{PQ} \equivd (\M_{SP}\vee \M_{PQ})\times (S\uplus Q)$, denoting the contraction operation by '$\times$'. In each case, we examine how to minimize the size of the `overlap' set $P,$ without affecting the right side entity. In the case of vector spaces, there is a polynomial time algorithm for achieving the minimum, which we present. Similar ideas work for graphs and for matroids under appropriate conditions. Next we consider the problem of decomposition. Here, in the case of vector spaces, the problem is to decompose $\V_{SQ}$ as $\V_{SP}\lrarv \V_{PQ},$ with minimum size $P.$ We give a polynomial time algorithm for this purpose. In the case of graphs and matroids we give a solution to this problem under certain restrictions.
item.dc:creator: H. Narayanan

item.title: Congestion-Aware Charging Coordination for Electric Ride-Hailing Fleets under Stochastic Demand
item.description: arXiv:2412.09978v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this study, we develop a dynamic charging scheduling method that integrates day-ahead charging planning and online reactive vehicle dispatch and charger assignment. The day-ahead planning model minimizes expected charging costs by considering anticipated waiting times and overnight energy replenishment costs. The online model then adapts this plan by maximizing the profit from vehicle dispatching and assigning vehicles to chargers through a reservation-based charging request scheduler to minimize the total charging-related operational time. The developed charging policy is tested on a Manhattan-like study area using synthetic data drawn from NYC yellow taxi data with a fleet size of 100 vehicles given the scenarios of 3000 and 4000 customers/day. The computational results show that our method outperforms different benchmark policies with up to +21.68% profit and +22.22% service rate for 4000 customers relative to the weakest benchmark. Sensitivity analyses are conducted for different system parameters, and managerial insights are discussed.
item.dc:creator: Tai-Yu Ma, Richard D. Connors, Francesco Viti

item.title: Split the Yield, Share the Risk: Pricing, Hedging and Fixed rates in DeFi
item.description: arXiv:2505.22784v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present the first formal treatment of \emph{yield tokenization}, a mechanism that decomposes yield-bearing assets into principal and yield components to facilitate risk transfer and price discovery in decentralized finance (DeFi). We propose a model that characterizes yield token dynamics using stochastic differential equations. We derive a no-arbitrage pricing framework for yield tokens, enabling their use in hedging future yield volatility and managing interest rate risk in decentralized lending pools. Taking DeFi lending as our focus, we show how both borrowers and lenders can use yield tokens to achieve optimal hedging outcomes and mitigate exposure to adversarial interest rate manipulation. Furthermore, we design automated market makers (AMMs) that incorporate a menu of bonding curves to aggregate liquidity from participants with heterogeneous risk preferences. This leads to an efficient and incentive-compatible mechanism for trading yield tokens and yield futures. Building on these foundations, we propose a modular \textit{fixed-rate} lending protocol that synthesizes on-chain yield token markets and lending pools, enabling robust interest rate discovery and enhancing capital efficiency. Our work provides the theoretical underpinnings for risk management and fixed-income infrastructure in DeFi, offering practical mechanisms for stable and sustainable yield markets.
item.dc:creator: Viraj Nadkarni, Pramod Viswanath

item.title: Real-Time GPU-Accelerated Monte Carlo Evaluation of Safety-Critical AEB Systems Under Uncertainty
item.description: arXiv:2604.27193v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Automatic Emergency Braking (AEB) systems represent a safety-critical national interest, with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS No. 127) requiring AEB in all new light vehicles sold in the United States by September 2029. However, production implementations frequently rely on deterministic stopping-distance or Time-to-Collision (TTC) thresholds that fail to capture uncertainty in sensing, road conditions, and vehicle dynamics. This paper presents a GPU-accelerated Monte Carlo framework for stochastic evaluation of emergency braking performance using a longitudinal vehicle model incorporating aerodynamic drag, road grade, brake actuator dynamics, and weight transfer effects. A one-thread-per-sample execution strategy exploits the independence of Monte Carlo rollouts, while deterministic CPU-generated sampling ensures bit-exact numerical consistency between CPU and GPU implementations. The framework is evaluated across four hardware platforms: two laptop GPUs (GTX 1650, RTX 5070) and two automotive-grade embedded platforms (Jetson Orin Nano, Jetson AGX Orin). Peak speedups of 54.57x are achieved. Real-time feasibility analysis with a complete AEB timing budget demonstrates that the Jetson AGX Orin can execute approximately 25,000 Monte Carlo samples within a 530 ms budget, enabling real-time probabilistic AEB evaluation as part of a complete embedded pipeline. Collision probability analysis demonstrates that a threshold set at the mean stopping distance of 79.2 m leaves a collision probability of approximately 47%, while the conservative 1% risk threshold requires a minimum safe headway of 111.1 m, an additional 31.9 m (40%). These results provide quantitative guidance for risk-aware AEB threshold selection under the NHTSA final rule.

item.title: Nonlocal Teams and Information Structures
item.description: arXiv:2606.08645v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We look at Bell inequalities from the lens of information structures in stochastic teams. We consider the usual Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) game and a dynamic variant of the same to study how various classes of strategies, classical, projective and quantum, behave under team theoretic solution concepts. We endow players with a fixed quantum state that we take as the Bell state, and allow variation of the measurement strategies. In the static game, projective strategies (where each player performs projective measurements) are team optimal for all parameter values and are closed under best response. In the dynamic game these properties fail: projective strategies may be strictly outperformed by classical ones, best responses to projective strategies need not be projective, and, beyond a sharp threshold on the channel noise, team optimal projective strategies cease to be person-by-person optimal, even though person-by-person optimal projective pairs always exist. These results shed light on the delicate interplay of information structure in quantum strategies and the fragility, under a change of information structure, of structural properties that are taken for granted in the static setting.
item.dc:creator: Drishti Baruah, Sachin Teli, Ankur A. Kulkarni

item.title: X-Safe: Embodiment-Agnostic Safeguarding for Robot Arm Manipulation Policies via Action Masking
item.description: arXiv:2606.22278v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Ensuring safety of learning-enabled robotic manipulation across diverse embodiments and tasks still requires significant manual engineering. For collision avoidance, existing approaches typically rely on embodiment-specific learned safety approximations or simplified robot models together with stopping-based fallback controllers that compromise performance. In this paper, we propose an embodiment-agnostic safeguarding approach, X-Safe, which provides formal probabilistic guarantees for collision avoidance without model simplifications or learned safety functions. By operating in the configuration space, our safeguarding method works with different types of robot policies. X-Safe reasons locally around the current configuration to establish safe regions and uses action masking to restrict the policy's support to these safe regions. We demonstrate X-Safe on two embodiments and three policies, both in simulation and on hardware. We observe less than half of the performance degradation compared to state-of-the-art safeguarding, and empirically corroborate our formal collision avoidance guarantees.
item.dc:creator: Alex Beaudin, Hanna Krasowski, Kartik Nagpal, Sanjit A. Seshia, Murat Arcak, Negar Mehr
